subject: ventures/mobile-oil-change-route-profit-calculator
professional: an independent mobile oil-change operator-owner with a CPA (what a week really nets after drive, oil, no-shows, fixed cost and tax) and a franchise-consultant view for the solo/franchise/employed comparison

evidence.correctness: Ran plan(sampleInput()) and recomputed in a separate Python script from the stated model (not from calc.mjs): revenue 2668.00 (0.92*(12*70+10*110+4*240)), supplies 1292.60, mileage 182.00 (26 stops*10mi*0.70), weekly fixed 132.69, work hours 26.61 (8.67 drive + 14.94 on site + 3 restock), solo net 1060.71, after-pay 262.39, profit/hour 39.86, franchise net at +20% volume and 8% fee 1043.26, employed net 506.21, break-even scale 0.459 (17.4 scheduled vehicles after rounding). All matched the tool to the cent. Per-type profits (4.72, 14.22, 5.40 per vehicle) re-weighted by completed vehicles sum to the 262.39 after-pay total. Independent of the author's tests but not checked against an external published standard (there is none for this model), so capped at 3.
evidence.completeness: Checked each README claim on the page/logic: profit per job and per hour with drive (works), break-even (works), target-margin price per type (works, advice flags the three sample types at 93.26/136.83/78.00), no-show cost (works), fleet batching table (works), solo/franchise/employed with equal-fee 7.5% and equal-wage 40.84 (works, tested to equalise), volume table, share link, CSV download, usage opt-out all present in index.html and calc.mjs. Not-modelled list is stated. No stubs or TODOs found.
evidence.verification: node --test calc.test.mjs page.test.mjs usage.test.mjs: 35 pass, 0 fail. Seeded three mutations one at a time and reverted each with git checkout: franchise keepShare /100 -> /10 (2 tests failed), insurance /52 -> /48 (8 failed), supplies not scaled by show rate (8 failed). All caught. git status clean afterwards. Tests are hand-arithmetic and round-trip identities, not property or boundary-heavy, but they bite.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (all), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, index.html head/script. Clean pure-function module, input validation with plain messages (negatives, NaN, integer counts, ranges), share link allow-listed to known keys. Defects: fixed cost is split equally per completed vehicle in typeLine (not by time or revenue); non-multiple fleetQty/batch silently yields fractional stops; sampleInput franchiseFeePct 8 / employedWage 20 differ from the readInput defaults 30 / 24, so the example and blank-field behaviour disagree; fixedCosts returns both rounded and unrounded fields.
evidence.claims: README, VENTURE.yaml, llms.txt and page claims checked against files: disclaimer and no-warranty text in index.html (footer line 155, note line 47) and asserted in page.test.mjs; 'nothing uploaded' backed by a test that bans fetch/XHR/sendBeacon; local-only usage counts backed by usage.mjs and usage.test.mjs; 'defaults are placeholders' stated. Flaws: llms.txt links to the retired duncan-haywood.github.io address (still redirects, but stale); canonical is the relative './index.html', not an absolute URL. VENTURE.yaml stage is honestly 'prototype'. No fake reviews or unbacked numbers.
evidence.fitness: Walked an operator's job: enter 12 conventional, 10 synthetic, 16 fleet vehicles; output says the week nets 1,060.71 cash but only 9.86 per hour after valuing own time, and that all three prices are below a 30% margin target. That answers 'what should I charge' and 'is batching worth it'. Gaps an operator hits in the first hour: only three fixed service types (no diesel, high-mileage, add-on sales such as wipers or air filters), no per-day schedule or multi-van, no sales tax or self-employment tax, no vehicle depreciation beyond a per-mile figure, flat fixed-cost allocation per vehicle.
evidence.domain: Compared with how a CPA or small-business adviser would cost a route service. Departures: (1) the no-show annual cost (8,598.72) adds drive/curb time valued at the owner rate AND the lost service margin (119.60 a week), which counts the same hour twice when the time rate is an opportunity cost; and it multiplies by 52 weeks with no holidays. (2) The solo vs employed vs franchise comparison is pre-tax: solo carries self-employment tax and no benefits, an employee does not, so the comparison favours solo. (3) Fixed costs are allocated equally per vehicle rather than by time. (4) The franchise model lets a fee be a flat percent of revenue and ignores initial franchise purchase and royalties on supplies. Good: drive time and mileage per stop are charged, batching is modelled with batch-wide no-show loss, and used-oil regulation is explicitly excluded.

defects.what: No-show headline cost (failedCostYear) counts drive and curb time at the owner rate and also the lost service margin, a partial double count, then multiplies by 52 weeks
Solo vs franchise vs employed comparison is pre-tax and ignores self-employment tax and benefits, biasing it toward solo
Fixed cost is allocated equally per completed vehicle, not by time or revenue, which skews per-type margin and target price
llms.txt links to the retired github.io host; canonical tag is a relative path
sampleInput franchise fee (8) and wage (20) differ from readInput defaults (30, 24)

verdict: A small, honest, arithmetically correct calculator: six headline outputs recomputed independently match to the cent, 35 tests pass and all three seeded bugs were caught, the page and README claims are backed by files, and the disclaimers and non-modelled list are clear. It meets the bar mainly on correctness, verification and claims. It falls short of a professional's sign-off on domain and fitness: the annual no-show cost partly double counts time, the three-way comparison ignores self-employment tax, and fixed costs are allocated flatly. The data is a three-type model with placeholder defaults, so an operator gets a useful planning view, not a tax-ready decision. Scores are before any fix.
